🧊 The ARK Vault, in 3D

The library computer built into a 50 cal ammo can, to scale: the battery at the hinge end with the wall charger set on top of the solar controller in front of it; the receipt printer on a printed riser at the latch end, the crank radio in front of it and an iPhone standing between the two; and the Raspberry Pi on the lid, which stands it up and switches everything on when you open it. Drag to turn it, right-drag or drag with two fingers to move it, and pinch or scroll to zoom.

What you're looking at

  • Open the lid and the Pi, on a printed base taped under the lid, stands up in the air. Flip the red power switch (in front of the printer) and the library starts. Flip it off when you're done: that just cuts the power, which is always safe because the Pi's memory card is read-only. A small thumb drive in the Pi's USB port has about 19 mm of room.
  • Only two parts are printed: the Pi's base on the lid and the printer's riser. Nothing lines the can.
  • The battery stands at the hinge end, straight on the floor's bump, rubber boots on its terminals.
  • In front of it, against the hinge wall: the solar controller standing on its edge on the floor, with the wall charger set straight on top of it, its mains cord coiled on top and the plug lying on the coil, to pull out when charging. The charger's battery leads come up to a quick-connect plug on top of the charger, then go over the battery to its terminals.
  • At the latch end, the printed riser holds the printer at the top, just under the Pi, and in front of it, at the same height, the volt/amp meter, the red power switch and the meter's button (a small switch set flush in the print; press its red button): hold it to check the battery. On the riser's floor, under the printer: the 12 V to 5 V converter that powers the Pi, and the fuse holder.
  • The radio stands in front of the riser, partly under the meter, and the iPhone stands on its end against the front wall. To take the radio out, lift the phone out, slide the radio toward the front wall, then lift it.
  • Wires: red is battery plus, through the fuse and the power switch to the 5 V converter and the printer; black is minus, through the meter. The converter's 5 V pair and the printer's USB lead go up beside the battery, over its top to the hinge, loop up into the lid and run along it to the Pi: the 5 V pair to the Pi's 5 V pins, the USB lead to a USB port. The solar controller isn't wired: it's only stored in the can, to take out and wire up after an event.
  • How to build it, the parts list, the wiring and the print files: the ARK Vault guide.
